# Graph

**Package** `telividb.graph.v1`

## Services

### `Graph`

Manages edges and traverses the graph they form.  The engine beneath this — edge storage, rehydration into an in-memory graph, and hop-bounded traversal with type filtering — is built and tested. Nothing could reach it until this service existed.

| Method | Request | Response | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CreateEdge` | `CreateEdgeRequest` | `Edge` | Creates an edge. |
| `GetEdge` | `GetEdgeRequest` | `Edge` | Retrieves a single edge. |
| `ListEdges` | `ListEdgesRequest` | `ListEdgesResponse` | Lists edges. |
| `BatchCreateEdges` | `BatchCreateEdgesRequest` | `BatchCreateEdgesResponse` | Creates several edges in one request. |
| `DeleteEdge` | `DeleteEdgeRequest` | `Edge` | Soft-deletes an edge. Returns the tombstoned edge. Deleting from the graph is reversible until expiry, which matters more here than elsewhere: an edge is often the only record that two things were ever related. |
| `TraverseGraph` | `TraverseGraphRequest` | `TraverseGraphResponse` | Traverses the graph outward from a set of seeds. Bounded best-first expansion, not a search over all paths. Each hop depends on the last, so this runs on the host rather than a device, and the bounds — hop count, result ceiling, per-hop decay — are what keep it from becoming the most expensive thing in a query. |
| `CreateEdgeType` | `CreateEdgeTypeRequest` | `EdgeType` | Creates an edge type, declaring the default weight its edges take. |
| `GetEdgeType` | `GetEdgeTypeRequest` | `EdgeType` | Retrieves a single edge type. |
| `ListEdgeTypes` | `ListEdgeTypesRequest` | `ListEdgeTypesResponse` | Lists edge types. |
| `DeleteEdgeType` | `DeleteEdgeTypeRequest` | `EdgeType` | Soft-deletes an edge type. |

## Messages

### `Edge`

A typed relationship between two resources.  Edges relate resources by name, never by internal ordinal: an ordinal is segment-local and means nothing outside the process that produced it, so an edge carrying one could not survive an export or a compaction.  This one type carries both kinds of relationship in the model — the semantic ones a retrieval follows, and the containment ones that place a conversation in a session or a session in a space. Keeping them in one graph is what lets a visibility predicate and a traversal be answered by the same structure rather than by two that must agree.

| Field | Type | # | Behavior | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | 1 | `IDENTIFIER` | Resource name of the edge. |
| `source` | `string` | 2 | `REQUIRED` | Resource this edge points from. |
| `target` | `string` | 3 | `REQUIRED` | Resource this edge points to. |
| `edge_type` | `string` | 4 |  | The type of relationship, such as `FOLLOWS` or `IN_SPACE`. |
| `weight` | `float` | 5 | `OPTIONAL` | Declared strength of this particular relationship. A prior about what this link is worth, overriding the default its type supplies. Weights multiply along a path rather than adding, so two hops through weak edges rank below one hop through a strong one — addition would let a long chain of weak links accumulate into a false strong signal. |
| `strength` | `float` | 6 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | How live this path is, as a time-decayed count of traversals. Learned evidence, kept separate from `weight` so reinforcement never overwrites the declared prior. Decayed rather than raw because a hundred traversals a year ago and three yesterday are not the same signal, and a separate recency factor over a raw count would double-count age. Accumulated in the resident graph and flushed periodically. The flush is allowed to lose recent increments: this ranks results, it does not audit them, and making every read a durable write would serialize the read path. |
| `last_traverse_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 7 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When this edge was last traversed. |
| `suppressed` | `bool` | 8 | `OPTIONAL` | Whether traversal stops here. A suppressed edge is a hard stop rather than a low score. The content it leads to is retained and its owner can still reach it deliberately; it is excluded from recall, and its existence remains visible to a caller assembling context so an agent knows what not to raise. |
| `create_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 9 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the edge was created. |
| `delete_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 10 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the edge was soft-deleted, or unset while it is live. |
| `expire_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 11 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When a soft-deleted edge is purged and becomes unrecoverable. |
| `etag` | `string` | 12 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Opaque value for optimistic concurrency on update. |

### `EdgeType`

A declared kind of relationship, carrying the default weight its edges take.  Declaring the default once means an edge of a given kind inherits a priority instead of every edge carrying its own magic number.

| Field | Type | # | Behavior | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | 1 | `IDENTIFIER` | Resource name of the edge type. |
| `display_name` | `string` | 2 | `OPTIONAL` | Human-readable name. |
| `default_weight` | `float` | 3 | `OPTIONAL` | Weight edges of this type take unless they override it. |
| `structural` | `bool` | 4 | `OPTIONAL` | Whether edges of this type express containment rather than meaning. Containment edges place a conversation in a session or a session in a space. They are followed when resolving what a principal can see and are not followed when expanding a retrieval, because membership is not a semantic relationship and would otherwise pull in every sibling. |
| `create_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 5 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the edge type was created. |
| `delete_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 6 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the edge type was soft-deleted, or unset while it is live. |
| `expire_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 7 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When a soft-deleted edge type is purged and becomes unrecoverable. |
| `etag` | `string` | 8 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Opaque value for optimistic concurrency on update. |

### `BatchCreateEdgesRequest`

Request message for creating several edges at once.  Edges import in a second pass, after the resources they join exist. A batch is how that pass is expressed, and one dangling edge follows the configured policy rather than silently disappearing.

| Field | Type | # | Behavior | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `parent` | `string` | 1 |  | Organization the edges belong to. |
| `requests` | `repeated CreateEdgeRequest` | 2 | `REQUIRED` | The individual create requests. |

Response message for creating several edges at once.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `edges` | `repeated Edge` | 1 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | The edges that were created. |

### `TraversalResult`

A resource reached by traversal, with the path that reached it.

| Field | Type | # | Behavior | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resource` | `string` | 1 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | The resource that was reached. |
| `score` | `float` | 2 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Combined score after applying edge weights and the per-hop decay. |
| `hop_count` | `int32` | 3 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | How many hops from the nearest seed. Zero means the seed itself. |
| `path` | `repeated TraversalStep` | 4 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | The path taken, so a result can be cited rather than merely returned. Provenance, not diagnostics: an assembled answer that cannot say how it reached a fact cannot be verified, which for a memory system is most of what it is worth. |

### `TraverseGraphRequest`

Request message for traversing the graph from a set of seeds.

| Field | Type | # | Behavior | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `parent` | `string` | 1 |  | Organization whose graph is traversed. |
| `seeds` | `repeated string` | 2 | `REQUIRED` | Resources to start from. |
| `max_hop_count` | `int32` | 3 | `OPTIONAL` | How many hops to expand. Zero selects a server-chosen default. |
| `edge_types` | `repeated string` | 4 |  | Edge types to follow. Empty follows every non-structural type. |
| `decay` | `float` | 5 | `OPTIONAL` | Per-hop score multiplier. Without a decay a node with many neighbours contributes all of them at its own score, and the graph half of a retrieval swamps the similarity half. |
| `max_result_count` | `int32` | 6 | `OPTIONAL` | Ceiling on resources returned, so a hub cannot become the whole answer. |
| `use_strength` | `bool` | 7 | `OPTIONAL` | Whether learned traversal strength contributes to the score. Defaults to false, leaving existing behaviour unchanged until asked for. When enabled, an untravelled edge still scores at a prior rather than at zero — otherwise a new edge could never be traversed, so it could never earn a count, and the trap would close on itself. |

### `TraverseGraphResponse`

Response message for traversing the graph.

| Field | Type | # | Behavior | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `results` | `repeated TraversalResult` | 1 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Resources reached, highest score first. |
| `suppressed_edge_count` | `int32` | 2 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Edges skipped because they are suppressed. A count, never the edges themselves. The caller assembling context learns that a region was avoided so it can decline to pursue the topic; the person being protected must not be handed the reminder, which is the harm suppression was asked for. |
| `complete` | `bool` | 3 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Whether every part of the graph could be consulted. False when a locked space held part of the path. A caller must be able to tell "nothing is there" from "something is there that you cannot currently see". |
| `locked_spaces` | `repeated string` | 4 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Spaces skipped because they are locked. Names only, never contents. |
